instruction: SAFETY/BYPASS-lens R2 review of WP-SCP-022 slice 020M post-fix-round-1. Branch: feature/wp-scp-022-020m-supply-chain-hashes. R1 HEAD: ee32abc. R2 HEAD: 4be0043. Read FIX-ROUND-1.md for closure narrative + prior review-safety.json for R1 findings. R2 mandate: (a) verify each R1 safety finding closed; (b) verify no new safety findings. Specific verifications: (1) SAFE-MAJ-002 (runner-preinstall bypass) closure: the unconditional install + version-pin assertion pattern at all 4 policy-check.yml sites + 1 release-gate.yml site actually defends against the runner-preinstall pyyaml 6.0.1 case. Verify by reading `gh run view 25232007939 --log` for run 25232007939 (PR #84 fix-round-1 commit); the install step should show pip downloading pyyaml-6.0.2 wheel + verifying hash + installing to ~/.local/lib... and the assertion step should show 'yaml=6.0.2 jsonschema=4.23.0' or similar success-path output. CRITICALLY: ensure the workflow doesn't have a NEW silent-skip path. (2) SAFE-MAJ-001 (CODEOWNERS gap) closure: requirements/** + docs/releases/** added before /CODEOWNERS self-protection line. Verify ORDERING INVARIANT preserved: list all CODEOWNERS rules in order from top to bottom and confirm specific governance rules ARE before broad wildcards (none added) ARE before /CODEOWNERS self-protection. (3) SAFE-MIN-001 (docs/releases/** CODEOWNERS) closure: same edit; verified with SAFE-MAJ-001. (4) SAFE-MIN-002 (workflow-selftest trigger) closure: requirements/** added to .github/workflows/workflow-selftest.yml `pull_request.paths`. Verify YAML syntax + path-pattern correctness. The Renovate auto-bump scenario: a future PR that touches only requirements/policy-check.txt should now trigger workflow-selftest. (5) SAFE-MIN-003 (conflict-gate.yml unhardened pip install) closure: TF-020M-001 filed in STATUS.md. Verify the TF entry's content: it correctly identifies the line and pattern (line ~42, `pip install pyyaml>=6.0`); the closure path is concrete (sibling lockfile or shared lockfile); the v1.1.0 candidate framing is appropriate. (6) NEW SAFETY SURFACE introduced by fix-round-1? The unconditional install on every workflow run downloads from PyPI on every PR. PyPI is generally reliable but if rate-limited / down, the workflow now fails closed. Is this acceptable? (Pre-020M state: same dependency on PyPI; only the install location/conditional differs. The fix-round-1 change does NOT introduce a NEW dependency on PyPI availability — that was already there for cold-cache runs.) (7) NEW SAFETY SURFACE: the version-pin assertion uses Python's `__version__` attribute which is set by the package itself. A malicious wheel that passes the SHA256 check but lies about its `__version__` would not be caught by the assertion. However, SHA256 verification is the primary defense — assert is a defense-in-depth secondary check. Confirm this layered framing is correctly described in FIX-ROUND-1.md and ADOPT-001 §12.7.13. (8) NEW SAFETY SURFACE: ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 now describes a regeneration command using `/tmp/scp-piptools/`. /tmp is shared multi-user on shared systems. For an ADOPTER following the documented procedure on a shared box, an attacker with write access to /tmp could replace the venv between creation and pip-tools install. Is this a realistic concern for the adopter audience (typically running on ephemeral CI runners or single-user dev machines)? Flag only as a nit if at all; not a real exploit path. (9) Cross-workflow drift defense: with the version-pin assertion in place, if a future PR bumps requirements/policy-check.in pyyaml pin to 6.0.3 without updating the assertion `yaml.__version__ == '6.0.2'` — the workflow would fail with the version-mismatch error. Verify this pre-merge enforcement is documented (in FIX-ROUND-1.md or ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 — the regeneration procedure should warn maintainers to update the assertions in lockstep). FILE A NEW TF if not documented. Per WP-SCP-022 §4.3. Return SonnetReviewResult JSON. NEVER recommend descoping.
